title: Prophecy Against the Shepherds of Israel

questions.question: Who does the Lord tell Ezekiel to prophesy against in chapter 34?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:2 (ESV): "Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel; prophesy, and say to them, even to the shepherds, Thus says the Lord God: Ah, shepherds of Israel who have been feeding yourselves! Should not shepherds feed the sheep?"

questions.question: What have the selfish shepherds of Israel been feeding instead of the sheep?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:2 (ESV): "Ah, shepherds of Israel who have been feeding yourselves! Should not shepherds feed the sheep?"

questions.question: What did the false shepherds do with the fat, the wool, and the fat sheep?
options: You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool, you slaughter the fat ones, but you do not feed the sheep
They gave them to Babylon as a tribute
They burned them all in sacrifices
They sold them in the markets of Tyre
questions.correctAnswer: You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool, you slaughter the fat ones, but you do not feed the sheep
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:3 (ESV): "You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool, you slaughter the fat ones, but you do not feed the sheep."

questions.question: Which of the following did the bad shepherds FAIL to do?
options: Heal the sick and bind up the injured
Bring back the strayed and seek the lost
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:4 (ESV): "The weak you have not strengthened, the sick you have not healed, the injured you have not bound up, the strayed you have not brought back, the lost you have not sought..."

questions.question: How did the selfish shepherds rule over the flock?
options: By giving the flock to foreign shepherds
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:4 (ESV): "...and with force and harshness you have ruled them."

questions.question: What happened to the sheep because there was no true shepherd?
options: They were scattered, and they became food for all the wild beasts
They starved to death in the pens
questions.correctAnswer: They were scattered, and they became food for all the wild beasts
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:5 (ESV): "So they were scattered, because there was no shepherd, and they became food for all the wild beasts."

questions.question: God says, "Behold, I am against the shepherds, and I will require my sheep at their hand..." What else will God do?
options: "I will rescue my sheep from their mouths, that they may not be food for them."
"I will throw the shepherds into the fire."
"I will turn the shepherds into sheep to be slaughtered."
"I will let the wolves devour the shepherds."
questions.correctAnswer: "I will rescue my sheep from their mouths, that they may not be food for them."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:10 (ESV): "and put a stop to their feeding the sheep... I will rescue my sheep from their mouths, that they may not be food for them."

questions.question: Who does the Lord God say will search for His sheep and seek them out?
options: "I, I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out."
A new generation of earthly kings
questions.correctAnswer: "I, I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:11 (ESV): "For thus says the Lord God: Behold, I, I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out."

questions.question: Where will God bring the scattered sheep, feeding them on the mountains by the ravines and in all the inhabited places?
options: To the green pastures of Eden
To the lush valleys of Egypt
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:13 (ESV): "And I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the countries, and will bring them into their own land."

questions.question: But God adds that He will also judge between sheep and sheep. Why is He judging the strong and fat sheep?
options: Because they push with side and shoulder, tread down the pasture, and muddy the water with their feet
Because they stole the shepherds' crooks
Because they led the flock out of the fold
questions.correctAnswer: Because they push with side and shoulder, tread down the pasture, and muddy the water with their feet
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:18-21 (ESV): "Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture, that you must tread down with your feet the rest of your pasture... you push with side and shoulder, and thrust at all the weak with your horns..."

questions.question: Who will God set up over them as one shepherd, to feed them and be their shepherd?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:23 (ESV): "And I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he shall feed them: he shall feed them and be their shepherd." (This is a messianic prophecy of Christ, the descendant of David).

questions.question: What kind of covenant will God make with the flock when He rescues them?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:25 (ESV): "I will make with them a covenant of peace and banish wild beasts from the land, so that they may dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods."

questions.question: When they dwell securely, what will God cause to come down in their season?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:26 (ESV): "I will send down the showers in their season; they shall be showers of blessing."

questions.question: What shall the people know when God breaks the bars of their yoke and delivers them from those who enslaved them?
options: That the prophets told the truth
That the king of Babylon was defeated
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:27 (ESV): "...when I break the bars of their yoke, and deliver them from the hand of those who enslaved them. Then they shall know that I am the Lord."

questions.question: How does chapter 34 conclude by describing the identity of the sheep?
options: "And you are my sheep, human sheep of my pasture, and I am your God, declares the Lord God."
"You are a holy nation, separate from all others."
"You are the descendants of Abraham, heirs of the promise."
"You are the lost tribes, found at last."
questions.correctAnswer: "And you are my sheep, human sheep of my pasture, and I am your God, declares the Lord God."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:31 (ESV): "And you are my sheep, human sheep of my pasture, and I am your God, declares the Lord God."

key_verse_text: "For thus says the Lord God: Behold, I, I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out."
